title: Two People, One Evening
description: Two people share a conversation at a busy café. Discover what each notices, try a respectful response, and see what can change when they ask rather than assume.

accessibility.summary: An untimed illustrated café story with choices, two accessible perspective tabs, and three possible outcomes. All images have text descriptions. No scores or time limits; you can leave or skip.
accessibility.notes: Eleven original sepia-toned illustrations with text alternatives. All decisions and consequences are explained in text. Open both perspective tabs before continuing.

assets.alt: Tamsin smiles and talks with Ruben across a café table. Two coffees and a small vase sit between them.
A busy café surrounds the table. Tamsin looks away, touching the side of the head, while Ruben watches with concern.
Patrons fill the café behind Tamsin and Ruben. Tamsin looks down as Ruben looks over, unsure what has changed.
Tamsin rests a cheek on a hand and looks away thoughtfully while Ruben watches across the table.
Ruben gestures with open hands while speaking to Tamsin across their café table.
Tamsin and Ruben look at each other with relaxed expressions across their coffee cups.
Tamsin and Ruben both smile broadly while sitting across from each other with coffee.
Tamsin speaks with an open-handed gesture while Ruben listens at the quiet café table.
Tamsin and Ruben pause in thought with coffee in front of them; background tables are occupied.
Ruben speaks with open gestures as Tamsin listens across the café table.
Tamsin and Ruben exchange small smiles at the café table with a vase and two coffees between them.

learningObjectives: Notice how the same social setting can affect attention and comfort differently for two people.
Separate what someone did from a guess about their feelings or intentions.
Consider both people’s perspectives when a conversation changes.
Practice a clear question or request that respects the other person’s choices.
